evidence.description2: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
evidence.name: Personal & Professional Development
evidence.profile: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.

courses.contribution: Required first-year development with scholarly source evaluation and written argument.

evidence.description2: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
evidence.name: Research Methods & Statistics
evidence.profile: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.

courses.contribution: Designs empirical studies, creates instruments and analyzes results in R to support audience and media research.

Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.

courses.contribution: Applies fairness, privacy and accountability frameworks to AI and uses research-grounded podcast communication. It adds analysis of AI in public communication without claiming recommender engineering.

evidence.description2: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

evidence.name: Calling Bullshit
evidence.profile: Examines misinformation through philosophy, history, psychology and practical information evaluation. Students distinguish misleading discourse from related concepts, investigate cognitive and social vulnerabilities, and analyze pseudoscience, statistical misrepresentation and reasoning errors. Projects map a misinformation narrative's actors and circulation and produce a research-grounded myth-debunking video with an external interview.

evidence.description2: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. evidence.name: Ethics

Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

assessment: Preserved and strengthened two 24-course proposals internally, replacing general creative performance and leadership communication where more specific inquiry, misinformation or AI ethics is available. The first centres nonfiction narrative, cross-media interpretation, documentary and public storytelling. The second centres contested claims, media ethics, persuasion and democratic institutions, including AI accountability and a climate communication case. Their different required work and course choices make them meaningfully distinct. Basic Dutch contributes everyday language rather than advanced newsroom language. Visual and digital production is material within the first proposal; a third full route would rely on the same production resources and less relevant filler. Data and AI supply specific methods and public questions, without a dedicated data journalism or recommender track. The prerequisites on the external side prevent final comparability and alignment decisions.
knownLimitations: No required Dutch reporting sequence, specified newsroom assignments or joint equivalent of the VU thesis and colloquium. Optional research would require separate consideration. The current external curriculum gap bars a comparison disposition.
